topics.text:
Sensitivity / sensibilidad
Concept: Sensitivity asks which fraction of actual positive cases was detected: TP / (TP + FN). A false negative is an actual positive assigned another class. Use the supplied positive-class meaning, not a numeric-label convention.
KAFE grounding: machine.confusion_matrix uses actual-class rows and predicted-class columns in the sorted union of truth and predicted labels. A C-class matrix has C cells per row: the chosen diagonal is TP; the sum of its off-diagonal cells is FN. The positive class is not necessarily label 1 or the second class. If machine.recall_score is actually used, distinguish its macro recall over classes observed in y_true: it is not automatically positive-class sensitivity. With no actual positives, sensitivity is undefined and not estimable; an API zero-denominator convention is not detection evidence.
Optional next step: Reuse supplied counts or observations. Ask only for missing TP and FN counts, alternatively an actual matrix and its label order. Check the ratio and percentage before quoting them; do not introduce another metric as the next task.
Caveat: Sensitivity describes detected positives, not false alarms or performance on a different population.

Classifier comparison and error costs / comparacion de clasificadores
Concept: Compare models on the same cases with the same class meaning. Missed positives and false alarms have different consequences. A qualitative priority is a valid basis for describing the observed trade-off; exact cost weights are optional when a particular decision needs them. Costs can be informed by losses, review time or stakeholder evidence, not discovered from the confusion matrix or invented to force a winner.
KAFE grounding: Reuse the supplied per-model error counts and check them against each matrix. If quantitative costs are useful, FN times its cost plus FP times its cost uses shared units and the same per-error assumptions across models. Check the relevant positional API only for implementation help.
Optional next step: Help organize the supplied counts around the learner's existing priority. On a draft, affirm supported claims and identify at most one actual justification gap if present, without supplying a replacement conclusion; a sound draft needs no forced revision. Do not assume an unspecified starter classifier.
Caveat: A comparison on a small sample or a repeatedly used final test set has limits; discuss the relevant limit without making a new checklist.

topics.text:
Accuracy with unequal class frequencies / exactitud y desbalance
Concept: Accuracy is correct predictions divided by all evaluated cases. For a confusion matrix, add the diagonal for correct predictions and all cells for the denominator; check the ratio and percentage separately. When one class is common, high accuracy can coexist with missing many rare-class cases.
KAFE grounding: Metrics operate on labels, not unthresholded scores. Use the supplied class order and actual-class row to separate detected from missed cases of interest. A correct overall fraction does not answer that class-specific question.
Optional next step: Explain the immediate misconception using the supplied class counts or positive row. Do not automatically add precision, an API caveat or a cost exercise.
Caveat: Few minority cases make estimates uncertain; an overall score alone does not establish detection ability.

Evaluation beyond training data / evaluacion con datos no vistos
Concept: Training data influences fitted parameters; validation helps choose settings, and an untouched test sample estimates behavior after those choices. Fit preprocessing only on training data. State which data roles are known rather than infer them from reported scores.
KAFE grounding: machine.train_test_split returns an indexable MACHINE container, not a destructured Python tuple, and does not stratify automatically. Consult split and cross-validation contracts when code is needed.
Optional next step: If the requested population claim needs independence, ask only which observations influenced fitting or settings; reuse stated roles.
Caveat: An exhaustive finite-domain check supports behavior on that specified domain; it does not require inventing unseen inputs. A different population or continuous extension needs a defined domain, target rule and evidence.

Scores, thresholds and labels / puntajes, umbrales y etiquetas
Concept: A score and a class label differ. Apply the stated threshold rule to each score in its supplied input order, then compare each resulting label with its target before counting matches. Near-threshold scores alone do not imply random decisions or an optimization endpoint. A sigmoid-shaped score is not automatically a calibrated probability.
KAFE grounding: gesha.Model.predict can return nested batch outputs. gesha.Model.predict_label uses score >= 0.5 for a one-unit output and argmax for multiple outputs, with no custom-threshold argument. Identify the output shape and class meaning only when needed to interpret the supplied number.
Optional next step: Interpret the requested score or set of decisions. Ask for a missing threshold or class meaning only if indispensable; do not restart an already supplied experiment.
Caveat: Reported matching labels do not reveal training history, memorization, convergence or causal effects of a change.

Representation and nonlinear transformations / capacidad de representacion
Concept: A single affine score with a monotonic threshold has one linear boundary. It can match three of the four Boolean XOR cases, not all four. Composing affine layers without a nonlinear hidden transformation remains affine. A suitable nonlinear architecture can represent XOR; not every arbitrary hidden unit, width or activation combination can. Epochs, learning rate and seed change optimization within the chosen hypothesis class, not its capacity.
KAFE grounding: gesha.create_dense declares units, activation and input shape; gesha.sequential composes compatible layers. Internal hidden computation is distinct from returning a raw layer output to the DSL. Capacity does not guarantee convergence. Reported predictions do not establish training settings, memorization or a causal effect.
Optional next step: Answer the learner's current representation question and accept their proposed experiment. Explain a linear hidden layer's affine composition without adding unrequested construction code or a new multi-part design decision.
Caveat: An exhaustive check of a finite Boolean domain supports that defined task. Do not invent labels outside that domain without a target rule, or infer broader statistical generalization from matching scores. Preserve the learner's architecture and conclusion; do not provide solved weights or a complete assessed program.

Learning rate and unstable updates / tasa de aprendizaje
Concept: A gradient update subtracts a learning-rate-scaled gradient from the current parameters. Steps that are too large for the local loss geometry can cross a useful region repeatedly or diverge; very small steps can make progress slow. Mini-batch noise, feature scales, initialization, gradients and optimizer state also affect the observed curve, so an oscillating loss is a symptom to investigate rather than a unique diagnosis.
KAFE grounding: Compile a GESHA model before gesha.set_lr or model.set_lr. Use a positive learning rate even though the pinned setter does not reject every invalid sign. The optimizer/loss and accepted positional training calls come from the reviewed contracts; no invented optimizer factory or Python keyword argument is needed.
Optional next step: Explain the step size using the supplied loss trend. If the learner wants an experiment, invite one prediction about a smaller rate while keeping other conditions comparable; use their existing prediction if supplied.
Caveat: Lowering the rate is not guaranteed to repair an incompatible loss, bad target encoding, insufficient representation or data leakage. A smoother training curve alone does not establish better held-out performance.

topics.text:
Overfitting and validation / sobreajuste
Concept: Improving training fit alongside worsening validation behavior is a warning sign of adapting to sample details rather than improving behavior on the intended population. Compare compatible training and evaluation evidence on a defined population; temporal trends are one possible form of evidence, not a prerequisite. One score or successful execution does not establish either overfitting or its absence.
KAFE grounding: Actual validation data and the metric computed by the run matter when interpreting validation loss or early stopping. Regularization and stopping controls are options to reason about when relevant, not automatic guarantees.
Optional next step: Use the supplied domain and known data roles before asking for further observations; keep unknown training membership and settings unknown. For an exhaustive finite task, acknowledge what all defined cases establish instead of inventing new targets or calling it memorization.
Caveat: Distribution shift, split mistakes or noise can also widen a gap. Training and validation losses can include different regularization terms in this runtime; explain that only if those losses are being compared.
